title: Peru-Bolivian Confederation
capsule: The Peru-Bolivian Confederation (Confederación Perú-Boliviana) was constituted on 28 October 1836 under the protectorate of Bolivian president Andrés de Santa Cruz, who united Bolivia with the newly partitioned North Peruvian State and South Peruvian State. Santa Cruz aimed to recreate an Andean polity recalling the Inca empire, and the confederation won early military successes, including the defeat of a Chilean invasion at the Battle of Yungay's prologue engagements. However, Chile and Argentina viewed the union as a geopolitical threat; a second Chilean expedition under Manuel Bulnes defeated the confederation's army at the Battle of Yungay on 20 January 1839, forcing Santa Cruz into exile and dissolving the confederation, which formally ceased to exist by November 1839.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The boundaries of the confederation are derived from the pre-existing departmental boundaries of Peru and Bolivia and are reasonably well-documented; the dataset's to-year of 1840 captures the final dissolution phase.
